The modifications establish a new mechanism to restore the SME (Scalable Matrix Extension) registers when the system exits a suspend state. The function `sme_suspend_exit()` is defined in `fpsimd.c` and is responsible for writing the necessary values to the system registers. This function is then called in `suspend.c` during the CPU's exit from suspend, ensuring that the SME state is correctly reconfigured. The header file `fpsimd.h` is updated to declare the new function, allowing it to be used in the suspend handling code. Overall, these changes ensure that the SME configuration is preserved across suspend and resume cycles, addressing the issue of registers resetting to an architecturally UNKNOWN value.

1. explain how the bug occurs, including all code statements that are most likely to lead to the bug and why.

Here is the commit message:
arm64/sme: Restore SME registers on exit from suspend

The fields in SMCR_EL1 and SMPRI_EL1 reset to an architecturally UNKNOWN
value. Since we do not otherwise manage the traps configured in this
register at runtime we need to reconfigure them after a suspend in case
nothing else was kind enough to preserve them for us.

The vector length will be restored as part of restoring the SME state for
the next SME using task.

Fixes: a1f4ccd25cc2 ("arm64/sme: Provide Kconfig for SME")
Reported-by: Jackson Cooper-Driver <Jackson.Cooper-Driver@arm.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240213-arm64-sme-resume-v3-1-17e05e493471@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises because the fields in the SMCR_EL1 and SMPRI_EL1 registers reset to an architecturally UNKNOWN value upon exiting suspend. This means that if these registers are not explicitly reconfigured after a suspend, the system may not correctly restore the state necessary for tasks that utilize SME features, leading to potential failures or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
+void sme_suspend_exit(void)
+{
+	u64 smcr = 0;
+
+	if (!system_supports_sme())
+		return;
+
+	if (system_supports_fa64())
+		smcr |= SMCR_ELx_FA64;
+
+	write_sysreg_s(smcr, SYS_SMCR_EL1);
+	write_sysreg_s(0, SYS_SMPRI_EL1);
+}
+
 #endif /* CONFIG_ARM64_SME */
